# Introduction
Thanks for stopping by! My name is Judah, I'm a senior at Colgate University studying Mathematics and Computer Science. You stumbled onto my github pages website, which right now is acting as a small portfolio for some of the statistics coursework that I've completed at Colgate. The sidebar on the lefthand side of the page can be used to navigate through finished assignments for the respective courses. Throughout the fall 2026 semester I'll be updating the page with work from my current class, MATH 354: Data Analysis 1.

# AI Use Statement
In the meantime, you ought to know about the extent of AI use in my work, as well as my general approach to using generative AI tools. Given the growing concerns surrounding the negative effects of AI use on mathematics education [@CipolliAI] and the potential for AI use to complicate users capacity and willingness to consistently follow professional ethical standards such as those provided by the American Statistical Association regarding professional and methodological integrity as well as responsibilities to peers, study participants, and stakeholders [@ASA2022].

The extent of my AI usage largely depends on the scope and context of a project. In educational contexts, I largely restrict my AI usage to limited debugging, syntax assistance, and independent review for concepts I am struggling with. I used to be willing to do these tasks through only a little more effort on stack overflow, but since the collapse of it and similar sites with the rise of AI tools, the first line of information is increasingly generative. Although I have not consistently been explicit in my communicating my AI usage in documentation in the past, going forward I am adopting the AI appendix proposed by Cipolli in [@CipolliAI].

For personal projects, as well as in professional contexts where AI usage is either the explicit or implicit norm, I use generative tools more extensively for code writing. The extent to which I scrutinize the code depends on the both the novelty and the complexity of the task. Regardless of the situation, I acknowledge the ethical and methodological complexity of proper use of generative tools. As these tools continue to develop faster than our standards and regulations, thoughtfulness and self-awareness remain at least as important as willingness to adopt new technology.
